label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — The sink expression bar.toCharArray() at line 73 outputs data derived from request.getQueryString(). Although doSomething() performs a replacement of the last character with 'Z', this transformation is insufficient to sanitize HTML/XSS payloads (special characters like '<' and '>' remain unencoded). The resolved sink value depends on attacker-controlled input (param), which flows through to the response writer. Setting X-XSS-Protection to 0 further indicates reliance on client-side features rather than robust server-side encoding.

evidence.note: User input extracted from request.getQueryString() into param variable.
doSomething() called with param, returns bar.
Sink: bar.toCharArray() printed to response writer.
Transformation in doSomething replaces only the last character with 'Z', leaving rest of user input unencoded.
